guidance: A single-room sizing estimate, not a health guarantee: CADR ratings cover particles only, are usually measured at the top fan speed, and no air cleaner replaces source control and ventilation.
method: The page follows the EPA portable air cleaner sizing chart, which pairs a floor area with a minimum particle CADR at an 8 ft ceiling: 65 cfm for 100 ft² up to 390 cfm for 600 ft², or 0.65 cfm per square foot. Because that chart is tied to an 8 ft (2.4 m) ceiling, the page scales the rate in proportion to room volume, so a taller room asks for proportionally more clean air. It reports the minimum in cfm and m³/h, the equivalent air changes per hour (CADR divided by room volume), and the minutes to remove 90% and 99% of particles from a well-mixed single room, where concentration falls exponentially and 90% takes ln 10 room volumes of clean air. It also checks a cleaner you enter: the equivalent air changes it delivers, how many units the room would need at that rated CADR, the clearance times at that rate, and the largest floor area one unit covers at the entered ceiling height. The model assumes the cleaner runs at its rated speed, the air is well mixed and no new particles arrive while it runs. CADR is rated for particles only and is usually measured at the highest fan speed, gases and odours need an activated-carbon filter, and no air cleaner replaces source control and ventilation.

sources.title: US EPA, Guide to Air Cleaners in the Home — portable air cleaner sizing chart: 65 cfm for 100 ft² up to 390 cfm for 600 ft² at an 8 ft ceiling, higher ceilings need a higher CADR, and the CADR rating covers particles only at the highest fan speed
Wikipedia, Clean air delivery rate — CADR is the particle-free airflow in cfm measured under ANSI/AHAM AC-1 in a 1,008 ft³ test room, and the rating applies to particulate matter, not gases
